messages:
elaine_pm: Quick sync on rerank endpoint prioritization — sketched a prioritization matrix for incoming customer asks (top_k semantics, score outputs, truncation). Pasting the gist, want engineering + research input. TL;DR: customers want deterministic top_k + normalized scores.

sam_s: thanks, Elaine. two immediate contract questions: do we define top_k over the original candidate set, or over the candidate set after any context truncation? behavior differs for streaming/huge docs.

raj_engineer: perf-wise we should offer two modes: 'post-trunc' (cheap: truncate then rerank) and 'pre-trunc-strict' (expensive: rerank against full candidate set prior to truncation). default to post-trunc.

laura_research: score normalization options: raw logits, softmax(probabilities) across candidates, or min-max across the returned k. For downstream comparability I prefer softmax with optional temperature param. Also return raw scores for advanced users.

elaine_pm: Proposed API snippet (minimal):
```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "model": "redwood-rerank-1",
  "query": "text...",
  "candidates": ["doc1","doc2", "doc3"],
  "k": 10,
  "score_normalization": "prob",       // enum: raw | prob | minmax
  "truncation_mode": "post-trunc",    // enum: post-trunc | pre-trunc-strict
  "context_cut": "right"              // left|right|balanced
}
```

raj_engineer: Implementation note: softmax requires fp stability across quantized backends. We should return both `score` (normalized) and `raw_score` (model logit) when possible. Also document that `prob` may be computed client-side if users prefer logits.

sam_s: launch acceptance criteria proposal: 1) API contract doc published; 2) p95 latency under 350ms for k<=20 on dedicated tier; 3) cost not exceed 1.5x current embed+re-rank baseline; 4) integration tests + canary run.

laura_research: evaluation metric: consistency under truncation. target Spearman rho >= 0.9 vs full-doc ranking for k=10 on our benchmark set. Also check score calibration across datasets.

elaine_pm: FYI customer ask — Acme Retail wants: deterministic ranking for top_k across shards, normalized scores between 0-1, and an option to fall back to their cross-encoder if candidate_count < 50.

raj_engineer: Suggest param additions: `fallback_policy`: enum {none, cross_encoder_if_small_set}, and `strict_determinism`: boolean (if true we add deterministic sort tie-breaker by candidate_id).

sam_s: UX note: rename top_k -> `k` to match other endpoints. default `score_normalization` = 'prob'. Also add `explain` flag to return small debug payload for canary.

deploy-bot: canary plan created: rolling deploy to 10% of tenants, collect mismatch_rate and latency histograms, abort threshold = 2% mismatch or p95 latency > 500ms.

elaine_pm: I'll update the matrix and pick defaults (k=10, score_normalization=prob, truncation_mode=post-trunc, fallback_policy=cross_encoder_if_small_set). please :thumbsup: if you agree or send objections.

laura_research: :thumbsup:

sam_s: :+1:

raj_engineer: one more thing — docs should clarify semantics for "returned k < requested k" when candidate set smaller. explicit example helps.

elaine_pm: agreed. I added examples and a small decision table in the doc (link in #product-resources). planning to freeze API spec by EOW if no blockers.

laura_research: noted, will run truncation/resilience evals tomorrow and post numbers.

sam_s: I'll draft the perf targets and an infra plan for batching/k caching to keep costs down.

elaine_pm: great, thanks everyone.
